title: Agentic Deployment Without Governance Infrastructure: Measuring the Current Agentic Safety Gap

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: agentic AI governance is an urgent gap. Quantifying the fraction of deployments with adequate agentic-specific governance makes the problem concrete and motivates framework adoption.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: identifying public agentic deployments and checking against a specific 3-item checklist is accessible for CS students. The methodology is straightforward coding.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: 20-30 deployments, 3 governance checks each, compute fraction. Clear bounded methodology with enumerated output.

novelty.reasoning: The 2025 AI Agent Index (arXiv:2602.17753, 2026) directly documents technical and safety features of deployed agentic AI systems, revealing significant transparency gaps around safety, evaluation practices, and ecosystem interaction. The WEF published 'AI Agents in Action: Foundations for Evaluation and Governance' (2025) with a framework for mapping agent lifecycles and risk surfaces. AIGN's 'Agentic Governance Collapse' reports 81% of organizations lack governance for agent-to-agent interactions and 38.6% have deployed agents at scale. McKinsey published a playbook for deploying agentic AI with safety. The IAPP published 'AI Governance in the Agentic Era.' The proposed contribution—surveying 20-30 agentic deployments against a 3-item governance checklist—is substantially covered by the AI Agent Index which surveys deployed systems across six categories.
